claims.text: CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The modeling approach uses alloy composition, temperature range, and a thermodynamic database as key inputs.
Gibbs free-energy minimization is the mechanism used to determine thermodynamic equilibrium.
The proposed approach applies over 298–2000 K.
Predicted melting temperatures will be within 10 K of experimental values.
Predicted enthalpies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted entropies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted volume changes at melting will be within 2% of experimental values.
Predicted liquid-phase thermodynamic properties will be within 5% of experimental values.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing three to six principal elements.
Uncertainty in the thermodynamic database limits prediction reliability.
Limitations of Gibbs free-energy minimization contribute uncertainty to the proposed predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the average absolute deviation exceeds 15% for any measured property.
